properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 17 at 9:31AM EDT until October 20 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this evening to
4 AM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE MONDAY NIGHT... ...HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 11 PM THIS EVENING TO 4 AM EDT TUESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 17 at 9:04AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage today, then strong northeasterly winds will slow river flow
leading to a quick rise in levels. The river is forecast to reach
Moderate Flood Stage late Sunday to early Monday, with a steady
increase through Moderate Flood Stage forecast next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.3 feet, Many docks become submerged along the river
and in canals in the Astor community. Water enters yards of
properties on Bartram Road, Holiday Circle and along Wild Hog Road
on the Lake County side. In Volusia County, water encroaches yards
of homes on the river side of Alice Drive. No wake zones are in
effect from near the South Moon Canal to approximately 800 feet
south of the Riverview lodge. At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps
covered at South Moon Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's
Jungle Den. Water approaching sites closest to the river at Fish
Tales RV Resort and Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair
Street covered by river water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks
underwater at the Astor Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive.
Portions of Fox Road are covered with water nearest to the river.
Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud roads are underwater with yards
inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane. At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed
into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become
inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the
river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor
are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are
inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is
inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and
yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall
at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Saturday was 2.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early next
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Typhoon Watch issued October 17 at 10:39PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Tropical storm conditions, including winds of 34 to 63 knots,
are expected. Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or
more are possible.

* WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Onset of damaging winds beginning late tonight, continuing
into at least Sunday night, possibly longer if conditions warrant.

* IMPACTS...Destructive winds will produce dangerous seas that could
damage, capsize or sink vessels, along with drastically reducing
visibilities in heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move quickly
toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains subject to
change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal
waters, a bit south of Guam, with damaging winds moving into Tinian
and Saipan Waters tonight and lasting into at least Sunday evening.
Champi is expected to strengthen further as it approaches, then move
through the region as a category 4 super typhoon Sunday morning.
Seas are quickly rising, with significant sea heights reaching as
high as 25 feet during closest passage of Champi. Dangerous sea
conditions may continue into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for tropical storm
force conditions through Sunday night. Secure all vessels. Conditions
are expected to be extremely dangerous for small craft, and dangerous
for any vessels of larger size. As Typhoon Champi approaches the
Marianas, stay in safe harbor.

properties.areaDesc: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 17 at 10:39PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or more
are expected.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Damaging winds are occurring in eastern waters, and will
begin later tonight in western waters. Onset of destructive winds
after midnight with typhoon force winds early Sunday morning.
Damaging winds will continue into at least Sunday night, especially
if Champi slows down.

* IMPACTS...Destructive to typhoon force winds will produce
dangerous to deadly seas that could damage, capsize or sink
vessels, along with drastically reducing visibilities in heavy
rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move quickly
toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains subject to
change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal
waters, a little south of Guam, with damaging winds moving in late
tonight and lasting into at least Sunday night. Champi is expected
to strengthen further as it approaches, then move through the
region as a category 4 super typhoon Sunday morning. Seas are
quickly rising, with significant sea heights reaching as high as
35 feet near the eye wall of Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may
continue into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for the passage of a
category 4 typhoon Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions are
expected to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely dangerous
for any vessels of larger size. As Typhoon Champi approaches, stay
in safe harbor.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 17 at 4:38AM AKDT until October 20 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Monday to 4 AM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds could blow around unsecured objects and make
travel difficult. Light snow could lead to areas of blowing snow,
reducing visibility at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Following strong southerly winds north of
Trims Camp on Monday, moderate to heavy snow is expected to build
in late Monday through Tuesday and Wednesday as winds shift to
being out of the north. This Wind Advisory will be followed by a
Winter Storm Watch that will be in effect from late Monday through
Wednesday night.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 17 at 7:37AM CDT until October 17 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Alabama, northwest
Florida, and southeast Mississippi.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will be capable of downing additional
compromised trees which would result in renewed power outages in
vulnerable areas impacted by the extreme winds during Hurricane
Isaias. In addition, large debris piles from storm cleanup may be
blown about resulting in additional hazards to anyone nearby
outdoors along with potentially blocking previously cleared
roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Many trees are leaning over power lines,
homes, and roads in the impacted area. Frequent wind gusts between
35 and 40 mph will create dangerous conditions outdoors in the
vulnerable areas. Elsewhere, winds may result in large tree
branches downed and localized power outages.
properties.instruction:
Use extreme caution if you must travel or be outdoors. Remain alert
for potential falling trees and power lines, blown debris, and
additional damage to structures that remain compromised from the
hurricane.
